exam_structure.paper_name: Greece and Persia — Compulsory Period Study
exam_structure.overview: Q1(a)–(c) Discrete factual knowledge (4m, AO1); Q2 Outline historical events/features in continuous prose (6m, AO1); Q3 Unseen ancient passage + own knowledge on features/characteristics (10m: 5 AO1 + 5 AO3 — zero provenance evaluation expected); Q4 Same unseen passage + own knowledge on second-order concepts (15m: 5 AO1 + 5 AO2 + 5 AO3); Q5 Evaluative essay (20m + 5 SPaG = 25m: 10 AO1 + 10 AO2 + 5 SPaG).

consistentThemes: The interaction between the Persians and other cultures, particularly the Greeks, Egyptians and Babylonians
The personalities and priorities of Cyrus the Great, Cambyses II, Darius I and Xerxes I including their priorities on matters of religion and architecture

sections.title: Key Time Span 1: The rise of the Persian Empire under Cyrus the Great, 559–530 BC

topics.title: 1.1 Rise of Cyrus and the Conquest of Lydia
points: The background and accession of Cyrus
The conquest of Lydia

topics.title: 1.2 Babylon and Cyrus' Imperial Toleration
points: The conquest of Babylon
Cyrus' attitude towards conquered peoples and his liberation of the Jews

topics.title: 1.3 Pasargadae and the Death of Cyrus
points: The construction of Pasargadae
The circumstances of Cyrus' death

sections.title: Key Time Span 2: Cambyses II, Smerdis and the accession of Darius, 530–522 BC

topics.title: 2.1 Cambyses' Conquest of Egypt
points: Cambyses' conquest of Egypt

topics.title: 2.2 Cambyses and Egyptian Culture
points: Cambyses' attitude towards the Egyptians and their culture

topics.title: 2.3 Death of Cambyses and Accession of Darius
points: The circumstances of Cambyses' death
Darius' overthrow of Smerdis/Bardiya/Gaumata

sections.title: Key Time Span 3: The reign of Darius the Great, 522–486 BC

topics.title: 3.1 Pacification, Building Projects and Imperial Administration
points: Darius' pacification of the empire, including the restoration of control over Babylon
Construction of Susa, Persepolis and the Egyptian canal
Persian culture and religion under Darius
Darius' organisation and administration of the Persian Empire

topics.title: 3.2 Imperial Expansion and the Ionian Revolt
points: Persian expansion into the Aegean Sea; the campaign in India; the war with the Scythians
The Ionian Revolt, including its causes, course and consequences
Persian relations with Athens prior to the revolt

topics.title: 3.3 Expeditions of 493–490 BC and Marathon
points: Mardonius' expedition of 493–492 BC
The expedition to Greece in 490 BC and its aftermath

sections.title: Key Time Span 4: Xerxes I and the Greeks, 486–465 BC

topics.title: 4.1 Accession of Xerxes, Revolts and Invasion Preparation
points: Death of Darius and accession of Xerxes
The suppression of revolts in Babylonia and Egypt
Persian military organisation and fighting techniques

topics.title: 4.2 The 480 BC Invasion: Journey, Thermopylae and Athens
points: The invasion of Greece, including Persian preparation, the journey to Greece, the Battle of Thermopylae, the sack of Athens

topics.title: 4.3 Salamis, Building Projects and Eurymedon
points: The Battle of Salamis
The completion of Darius' building projects
The Battle of Eurymedon and Plutarch's 'famous peace'
